People who don't live here (or who haven't visited for any period of time) have no idea just how far out of the way the arena is from a large part of the metropolitan area *and* what a craphole that area around the arena has been for most of its existence. Don't get me started on the arena itself, either.

>opposing fans shouldn't be allowed to buy tickets Not online direct from the team, no. This allows the locals to get first dibs on the tickets. For the record, that was squat to  me. I had a presale code for the first batch of tickets released (9am) and those sold out in under 3 minutes. I didn't get any and nobody else I knew - locals - managed to score any direct from the team. Everyone I know, fan of this team or that team, has had to buy secondary market. In previous rounds, away fans were able to call the box office and acquire tickets directly without a problem. >represent their team when they happen to be playing in the building That's not what is going on here. Fans from the other city are welcome to wear their attire in all but 7% of the premium club/lounge seats in the arena and, I assure you, they will do so. There have literally been a handful of people impacted by this policy all playoffs and those were STMs of those seats who happen to have another team (a rival city or another major market, typically) as a "primary" team. I feel like I've tried to clarify this issue for months now. It's not a big deal. It hasn't had much of an impact. I'm a season ticket member who has attended every playoff game, so I probably have a better on the ground view on this than some random writer in that other city. The away team is **well** represented here.
